name: v1.0.275
body:
## ✨ New: `/ss` finds a past session from one sentence

You remember what a conversation was about, not which project, engine or week it happened in. `/ss` takes that half-memory and finds the session:

```text
/ss the session where we worked out CSRF on the local API
```

The agent does not search your sentence verbatim. It expands it into the words that would literally appear in that conversation — both languages for technical topics (`跨站` / `CSRF`), synonyms, the terms the assistant would have used — searches every session Cockpit can read across all projects, all engines (Claude, Codex, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, Ollama) and all dates, reads the snippets, and replies with 1–3 candidates. Each carries a session link; clicking it switches to that project and opens the session in the Agent panel.

Behind it, Cockpit keeps a text-only copy of each session's prompts and replies under `<data-dir>/search-corpus`, updated incrementally, and searches it with ripgrep, so two-character Chinese words like `快照` match. The first search on a machine takes a few seconds while that copy is built.

## ✨ New: `/dl` hands work to another session without waiting

Halfway through a task you notice work that belongs somewhere else — a flaky test in another repo, a job better suited to Codex. `/dl` starts it there and returns at once:

```text
/dl have codex fix the flaky date test in the api project
```

The agent writes a self-contained brief (the child sees none of your conversation), starts a new session in the target directory on the chosen engine, and repeats the receipt — engine, directory, link — in its reply before carrying on. The child is an ordinary session: open the link to watch it or take over. Later, ask how it went; the agent finds the receipt, in this conversation or through `/ss`, and reports `running`, `done`, `failed` or `incomplete` along with the child's last reply.

Nothing is stored server-side — status is read from the child engine's own transcript. At most 4 delegated sessions run at once (`COCKPIT_DELEGATE_MAX`); past that the request is rejected rather than queued.

## ✨ New: A Host / Origin check on every request

A web page open in your browser could previously reach a local Cockpit through DNS rebinding or a cross-site request. Every HTTP request and WebSocket upgrade now passes a check first: a request arriving over loopback must address Cockpit by a local host name, and a state-changing request or WebSocket upgrade that carries an `Origin` must be same-origin. Rejections are `403 Forbidden`. `curl`, the CLI and skills send no `Origin` and are unaffected.

**If you reach Cockpit through a tunnel (ngrok, cloudflared, …), this changes behaviour.** The tunnel connects over loopback with its public hostname in `Host`, so it is now refused unless you allow that name or run in token mode:

```bash
COCKPIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS=my-box.ngrok.app cockpit     # no token: anyone with the URL gets in
cockpit --token my-secret-value                    # token mode: the tunnel must forward X-Forwarded-For
```

Keep the tunnel's original `Host` header; if it is rewritten to `localhost`, POSTs and WebSockets get 403.

## 🐛 Fix: A one-time task that came due during a restart now runs

Scheduled timers die with the process, and a one-time task whose moment passed while Cockpit was down was marked completed without ever running — and then showed as failed in the panel, indistinguishable from a real failure. Such a task now fires on the next start if it came due within the last hour; older than that it is retired, marked unread, and logged. A task set with a zero-minute delay, which was retired on the spot for the same reason, runs too.

## 🐛 Fix: Session history for every engine, from any directory

Loading a session's history resolved the transcript against the directory Cockpit was launched from, so it failed for any session outside that directory — which is every session when the prod server starts outside a project — and it only ever looked in Claude's store, so Codex, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and Ollama sessions always 404'd. It now resolves by the session's own project and checks every engine's store.

## 🐛 Fix: Finished sessions sort above running ones

In the sidebar session dropdown, recent sessions and the mobile list, sessions that finished and are waiting for you to read now come before those still running.

## 📚 Docs: `/ss`, `/dl` and the Host check

The Skills guide covers `/ss` and `/dl`, the CLI reference documents the Host / Origin check with `COCKPIT_ALLOWED_HOSTS` and `COCKPIT_DELEGATE_MAX`, and a new post walks through both commands: [Find any past session with /ss, hand work off with /dl](https://opencockpit.dev/en/blog/find-and-delegate-sessions/).

name: v1.0.274
body:
## ✨ New: Codex streams its reply

Codex replies used to arrive as one block while every other engine typed. The cause was the transport, not the renderer: `@openai/codex-sdk` speaks only `codex exec --experimental-json`, whose event surface has no incremental text at any setting. This drops the SDK and speaks `codex app-server` directly, which publishes genuine fragments rather than cumulative snapshots — 30 text deltas where there was 1 block, and a "processing" counter that climbs continuously instead of sitting at 0 until the very end. The client needed no changes at all; the streaming path written for Claude takes Codex verbatim.

Tool calls now get a globally unique id from birth, recorded to disk, so a snapshot keyed by one is still findable after a reload. That retires five id resolvers, six per-turn counters and a shell-command fuzzy matcher which existed only because the old ids restarted at `item_0` every turn — measured over the real shadow repos before removal: 1489 (session, tool id) pairs, zero duplicates.

The rewrite surfaced a run of failures that all failed silently, now fixed: a failed turn reported as a clean success (failure rides on `turn/completed` — there is no `turn/failed`), a retryable error leaving the turn hanging until aborted by hand, every sub-agent bubble's live path being dead code from a snake_case mismatch, Codex turns having lost their todo list entirely, and a sub-agent finishing tearing its parent down mid-`wait_agent`. Stopping a run now asks before it kills: children are interrupted first, then the parent, and the process kill is only the bound.

Separately, a `thread/resume` that fails no longer restarts as a fresh thread in silence. When the ChatGPT desktop app holds a thread's writer lock, the server refuses every resume — you would get a second tab for what looks like one conversation and a model that had forgotten everything. That now lands as a system row naming both session ids and the engine's own message.

## ✨ New: The transcript holds your reading position

Three reports, one hole. A completed turn left half a screen of blank that nothing reclaimed; a tab you had switched away from came back with that blank frozen in place; and scrolling up during a stream was undone within 50ms, parking you at the top of the turn while text kept arriving. They were the same confusion: the reserved blank counts toward `scrollHeight`, so "the end of the scroller" and "the end of the transcript" differ by exactly one spacer, and the pin formula treated those two numbers as identical.

The spacer is now derived from the position being held rather than owned as state — exactly enough blank for that position, never a pixel more. It evaporates as the reply grows into it, a pin no longer has to be released with a jump, and no state can hold a blank that outlives the position that justified it. Sending still scrolls your question to the top and reserves the room below it, so the answer grows into blank instead of shoving the question off screen; a long user turn (a pasted SKILL.md, routinely) clips to 16 lines with a show-more toggle.

Your place now also survives leaving. A run that finishes while you are elsewhere no longer moves the viewport of the tab you come back to, and switching projects or reloading the page restores the tab you were on along with where you were in it. The policy is a pure reducer with property tests over 200 random event sequences, plus a regression test per report.

## ✨ New: Maximise a chat pane

Side by side splits the panel in half, and half of a narrow window is not enough to read a long turn in. Each pane gains a maximise button that blows one column up to cover the row, with the other keeping its layout underneath, so restoring is free. Switching tabs carries the maximise along with the focus rather than dropping out of it, and closing a split cannot leave a stale "maximised" behind to resurface the next time you ask for one.

## ✨ New: Context controls say what they keep, and a turn can be deleted

Forking from a message now spells out the difference: **Continue from here** keeps all context through that turn, **Only this turn** keeps just that question and answer. Plan mode is labelled read-only, and a new **No history context** mode sends each message to the model on its own with no prior conversation — the transcript above still records everything.

A turn can also be removed outright — the question, the answer and its tool records — from the message's own row. It asks first, and refuses while the session is running.

## ✨ New: Quick instructions, grouped and edited as text

Quick prompts become quick instructions and gain one level of grouping; a group opens as a flyout beside the popover. Both the global and the project list are editable as plain text — one top-level entry per line, lines beginning with `- ` after a group name become that group's instructions:

```
Continue
Draw with text
- Draw a login flow
- Draw a system architecture
```

Reads fall back to the old `prompts.json` and never write to it, so downgrading to an earlier build still finds its data.

The lightning bolt was saying three different things on screen at once. It now means only "quick instructions", in both the chat and console input bars. Recent sessions takes a history icon, scheduled tasks moves off the bare clock to an alarm clock, and skills gives up the star — that mark means "favourite" elsewhere — for a joystick.

## ✨ New: The message index moved onto the jump capsule

The list button sat in the composer toolbar, six icons away from the prev/next steppers that do the same job at a smaller scale. It now rides the bottom jump capsule, after a divider. The dialog itself was capped at `max-w-2xl`, wasting a wide display; it uses the same shell the session boards do, so width tracks the viewport and filtering no longer makes the dialog jump.

Jumping also looks like what it did. Selecting a message used to light a full-width rectangle with square corners, three times the bubble's width; the flash now lands on the turn itself, scrolls instantly rather than gliding across tens of turns (which ate the highlight's whole budget before arrival), and replays when you jump to the same row twice.

## 🐛 Fix: One badge per session, and it survives a refresh

Every session list carried its state twice — an 8px colour dot and the round number chip beside it, two glyphs and two colour families kept in step across five files. The chip keeps the job and the dot goes; unread drops from a near-solid red to the same restrained orange wash that loading uses, so running and done now differ by motion rather than hue, and no red reads as an error where none happened. The recent-sessions and scheduled-task counts use that one style instead of their own hand-rolled pills.

The state is also right again after a reload: a running tab keeps its indicator, the tab you were on comes back active, and recent sessions no longer lose the entries worth keeping. Project rows in the sidebar now show how many sessions they hold, with the active project's badges taking priority.

## 🐛 Fix: Sticky headers in Scheduled Tasks

Headers pinned in the scheduled-tasks panel leaked the content scrolling underneath them.

## 📦 Misc

Favourite moves off the tab bar and onto the chat toolbar, where the rest of the session's actions already are. `claude-agent-sdk` goes to 0.3.268 and `codex` to 0.154.0, both still exactly pinned — bumped by hand now that the scheduled bump workflow is retired.

name: v1.0.273
body:
## ✨ New: A diff opens beside the chat that produced it

Clicking "all file changes" used to swipe the Explorer into view and draw the diff over the FileBrowser — taking away the one thing you actually want next to a diff, which is the turn that wrote it. The diff is now a column inside the agent panel, sharing the row with the chat panes. Same viewer, one home instead of two.

A diff column and a second chat pane are the same right half of the panel, so they are mutually exclusive — but only by derivation, never by mutation. Opening a diff hides a split you built rather than destroying it, and closing the diff gives back the exact split that was there. On narrow screens the column can take the full panel width; the panes stay put underneath rather than being squeezed to nothing.

## ✨ New: Two chat panes, and they survive a reload

The agent panel splits into two panes with independent sessions. The layout is now persisted per project, so a refresh no longer silently collapses you back to a single pane — and a session closed in another browser tab leaves that pane blank instead of collapsing the split behind your back.

One composer serves both panes: the focused chat portals its input into a shared slot below them, so neither pane spends column height on it.

## ✨ New: Send a message to the other pane

In side-by-side mode, a message's hover row gains a fourth control between the excerpt scissors and the timestamp. It forwards that message's text to the other column and starts a run there immediately. The arrow points at the neighbour, so the button reads as a direction.

It sends the same plain text the copy button beside it would give you — no "forwarded from…" framing, since the receiving model reads framing as instructions — and it does not steal focus, because both panes are already on screen.

## ✨ New: The user-message list is the whole transcript now

The jump-to-message modal listed whatever the chat happened to have paged in (10 turns), so it was silently incomplete and clicking anything above that window did nothing. On one real session it showed 13 of 52 turns.

It is now served from disk: every human turn in the transcript, searchable, and selecting an unloaded row widens the chat window first so the jump actually lands. Timestamps show up for persisted rows (they were blank for everything but the current turn), and the jump highlight no longer flashes a white band around the bubble on the dark theme.

## ✨ New: Lean 4

`.lean` files were degrading quietly on four surfaces at once — no syntax highlighting, a generic grey file icon, line-level instead of block-level diffs, and no presence in the project graph at all. All four are fixed, including a `∀` file icon and theorem-level block diffs, which on a proof repo is the whole question you're asking a diff.

Validated against a 60,598-file formalization repo: 434/500 exact-name matches, zero mismatches, zero overlapping spans across 76,891 lines. Symbols only — import and call edges are deliberately not scraped, because Lean resolves lemmas by elaboration and a best-effort guess would render mostly-wrong edges as fact.

## 🐛 Fix: Large repos stop OOM-killing the server

Opening a very large repo could take the whole process down about four minutes after the first query — post-build analytics is fire-and-forget, and on an 809K-symbol index PageRank and the tf-idf pass peaked at 10 GB over an 8 GB heap, with 82 seconds of that synchronous and the event loop dead throughout.

Three bounds fix it. The file cap goes from 15,000 to 100,000 (`git ls-files` is alphabetical, so the old budget was exhausted inside the first directory and search returned zero hits for everything later in the alphabet — which reads as a broken feature, not as a cap). Analytics is skipped above 200K symbols, reporting a distinct reason so consumers stop retrying for a result that will never arrive. And the index cache is now LRU with a 1M-symbol budget, sized by bytes rather than entry count, instead of keeping every project you ever opened resident forever.

## 🐛 Fix: One node shape across the projectGraph API

`/api/projectGraph` spoke three vocabularies for the same concepts, so a parser written against one endpoint read `undefined` against another — the right number of rows, every field empty. Search now returns the canonical node with a real line range instead of the Cmd+K palette shape, `callees` calls its focal symbol `target` like its siblings, and co-edit rows agree on `filePath`. Co-edit history also gains a `probability`, so callers stop comparing a raw count against a ratio threshold.

## 🌐 Site: Crawlability, a real /docs index, and consistent naming

`robots.txt` was disallowing `/_next/`, hiding the CSS and JS Googlebot renders the page with. Every page shipped `<html lang="und">`, including the Chinese ones. 58 of 86 sitemap URLs carried no `lastmod`. The favicon and manifest 404'd. All fixed, with sitemap dates derived from real content — post dates, release dates, and the last commit that touched each docs file, recorded at author time rather than computed on CI, where a fresh clone would claim the entire site changed on every deploy.

`/docs` was a bare redirect stub, which under a static export compiles to Next's client-side error shell: 23 KB of HTML with no `<h1>`, no prose, and no `lang` — at a URL the homepage links to directly. It is now a real index page, with a card per docs page whose blurb is extracted from that page's own opening paragraph, putting all 26 docs pages one hop from the homepage.

The site also now says **OpenCockpit** on first mention throughout — docs openings, blog titles and descriptions, homepage copy — rather than the generic noun.

## 📦 Misc

Chat's prose surfaces finally have a typographic contract: a bounded reading measure, leading and scale shared by chat turns, the Explorer preview, review pages, the skills modal and the diff modal. User bubbles get a brand-teal border so their edge reads as a boundary on the dark theme. The website has a lint setup of its own instead of relying on `next lint`, which Next 16 removed.

name: v1.0.272
body:
## 🐛 Fix: Math renders in chat again

Chat bubbles have shipped with math rendering switched off for a while, because `remark-math` misread dollar signs in assistant prose — `Set $WORK, then $CMP` parsed as a formula, and `$500 and $1,200` swallowed the words between them. Turning the feature off made the misreads stop and took every real formula with it.

The guard is now an AST post-pass using the adjacency rules from `markdown-it-texmath` and KaTeX's auto-render, which lean on one property of real text: `$VAR` and `$500` are word-initial in prose, so a false positive's closing `$` is almost always preceded by a space. Running on the AST also means fenced blocks and inline code are immune for free — they were tokenised as code long before math is considered. A real Fermat's-Last-Theorem session renders 64 formulas with zero demotions while shell variables, prices and code blocks pass through untouched.

`\(...\)` and `\[...\]` are normalised to the dollar forms too. Models emit these constantly and `remark-math` supports neither, so until now they were dropped silently, with `\(` collapsing to a bare `(`.

The old workaround it replaces was corrupting text on its own: a malformed replacement string turned `$500` into `\$100`, and `$2 and $9` into `\$1 and \$1`, wherever math was enabled — the Explorer preview, review pages, and the standalone `/html-lib` markdown bundle. That's gone.

## ✨ New: Open and close browser bubbles from the CLI

`cockpit browser <id> <action>` could only drive a bubble you had already opened *and* clicked the shortId badge on, so every automation flow began by asking a human to click twice. The two missing verbs are here:

```bash
cockpit browser open https://example.com [--cwd PATH] [--wait-ms N]
cockpit browser <id> close [--cwd PATH]
```

No new control channel — `open` appends the same history entry the console writes when you type a URL into it, and the existing push makes every open UI materialise the bubble. The shortId it prints is live immediately, because entries now carry their own auto-connect flag instead of waiting for a badge click; that survives a reload, so a UI refresh mid-automation brings the bubble back still drivable.

`open` polls for that registration rather than assuming it and exits `2` when no UI applied the delta — with nothing connected the entry is merely persisted, and reporting success would strand you on a shortId that never answers.

## ✨ New: Compact code map folds unchanged lines inside a chip

精简 density in the code map was a block-level filter only: chips the diff didn't touch were dropped, but a chip that survived rendered every one of its lines. A 372-line function with a 4-line edit still cost 372 lines of scrolling — the exact thing the density switch exists to prevent.

Unchanged runs inside a chip now collapse to a single clickable bar (changed line ± 3, the same rule file view already uses for 精简, so flipping between 文件 and 代码地图 doesn't change what the word means). A click reveals that whole gap. Callee pins and the diff minimap follow the fold, so a pin whose call site is hidden parks on the bar rather than drifting out of alignment.

## 🐛 Fix: A sub-agent's own sub-agents

An Agent row inside a sub-agent transcript rendered with no drill-in at all, so a grandchild agent's work was unreachable from the UI. The lookup underneath was always depth-agnostic — every agent of a session writes its sidecar into one flat directory — and the row was simply missing the session id the entry is gated on. Dismissing a nested transcript also used to collapse every modal above it, since React bubbles portal events up the component tree rather than the DOM tree.

Nested rows now show running state as well. Neither of the two places task state normally lives can hold it — the spawning call is recorded in the sub-agent's own transcript, and a sub-agent's transcript records neither the structured launch receipt nor any completion notification — so for depth ≥ 2 the live event stream is the only source there is, and it now has a home outside the message tree. Rows subscribe individually, so a progress tick doesn't re-render a session whose bubbles can hold several hundred tool rows.

## 🐛 Fix: viewBox-only SVGs rendered blank in an image diff

On the working-tree side of an unstaged image diff, an SVG carrying only a `viewBox` resolved to zero width and the side came up empty. Raster images hid the bug behind their intrinsic size.

name: v1.0.271
body:
## ✨ New: GPT-6-Astra

Codex SDK 0.153.2 brings **GPT-6-Astra**. It's now at the top of the Codex model picker, with `low` reasoning as its default — the full `low → medium → high → xhigh → max → ultra` range is available from the traits row beside it.

GPT-5.6-Sol remains the application default, so nothing changes for existing sessions unless you pick Astra yourself.

## 🐛 Fix: A subagent's work is its own, not the parent turn's

One mistaken identity produced three symptoms, all of them in bubbles that launch subagents. The SDK forwards a subagent's tool calls on the parent stream, and Cockpit counted them as the parent's own:

- **Narration broke mid-word.** Every forwarded frame started a new message part, so streamed text was chopped into fragments and markdown was parsed per fragment — a `**bold**` split across two of them rendered as literal asterisks. Background agents made this the normal case: one measured turn showed 675 tool calls charged to a bubble whose transcript holds 52.
- **No spinner while a subagent worked.** "Does this tool call have a result" was doubling as "is the subagent still working", and since subagents went background-by-default an Agent launch answers in ~30ms with a receipt. Every Agent call in a measured transcript resolved in under 0.03s.
- **The drill-in modal never refreshed.** Same wrong signal gated its polling, so it fetched once on mount and only advanced if you closed and reopened it.

Task rows now carry the spawned work's own state, fed by the real `task_started` / `task_progress` / `task_notification` events and joined across the whole session — a backgrounded agent reports back long after its launch turn has ended. `running` is only ever written by a live event from the owning process, so a stale task can't revive itself during a later, unrelated run.

The spawning call still renders and still opens the real nested transcript. Nothing is lost.

## 🐛 Fix: Drilling into a Codex sub-agent said "no messages found"

Codex 0.153 moved the sub-agent activity line into a new envelope — same four fields, but the call id migrated from `event_id` to `item.id` and the discriminator from the payload's `type` to `item.type`:

```
0.147    {type:'sub_agent_activity', event_id, agent_thread_id, agent_path, kind}
0.153+   {type:'item_completed', item:{type:'SubAgentActivity', id, ...}}
```

That line is the only record binding a spawn to the thread it created, so its parser returning `null` took out both the drill-in and the Task bubble's result — for every Codex session Cockpit has produced since the SDK was pinned to 0.153. Every other Codex surface (exec, patch, MCP, web search, todo, error banners) kept working, which is how a routine SDK bump shipped this unnoticed.

Both envelopes are normalised now, and one verbatim line per era is pinned in the tests, copied off disk with only ids anonymised. The next time Codex moves it, a test fails instead of a drill-in.

## 📦 Misc: Bundled agent CLIs

Codex **0.153.2** (was 0.153.0) and Claude Agent SDK **0.3.260**.

name: v1.0.270
body:
## ✨ New: Claude Fable 5.1

Claude Code 2.1.257 shipped **Claude Fable 5.1** as the default Fable model. The model catalog is server-driven, so the SDK never gated it — but Cockpit keeps its own hardcoded lineup, which meant the picker didn't know it existed. `claude-fable-5-1` is now in the picker and in the `ultracode` / `xhigh` capability sets.

## 🐛 Fix: Six models were priced by guesswork in token stats

The pricing table only listed part of the lineup; anything missing fell through to a substring fallback that inferred a price from the model family. Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Sonnet 5, Mythos 5 and Mythos 5.1 all took that path. Only **Sonnet 5** was actually mispriced — billed at $3/$15 against a real $2/$10 — but the rest were correct by luck, not by table.

Fable/Mythos 5.1 read cache at $0.25/MTok, the one number in the table that can't be derived from the input price; the fallback would have overstated it 4x. Lookup keys also strip a trailing date suffix now, so `claude-opus-4-5-20251101` from an older transcript and the undated spelling stop missing each other.

## 🐛 Fix: A session could stay "thinking" for hours after the turn ended

A turn whose result had already landed stayed resident until every background task reported back, and two paths left that set permanently non-empty: one missed `task_started`/`task_notification` bookend, or an `ambient` housekeeping task that outlives the turn by design. The session held its input stream open and read, from the outside, exactly like a model still working.

Residency is now driven by the SDK's `background_tasks_changed` level signal rather than paired edges, with the edges kept as a fallback for older CLIs. The loading bubble also names what the turn is waiting on, instead of only counting elapsed seconds.

## 🐛 Fix: A failed Codex turn now says why it failed

Codex records the reason a turn died — capacity, rate limit, aborted stream — only on its `task_complete` line, and the CLI's non-zero exit doesn't carry it. The live banner read `Codex Exec exited with code 1: Reading prompt from stdin...`, and on reload the turn came back as its last tool call and nothing else, indistinguishable from an agent that simply stopped.

Both paths now render the real message: **⚠️ Selected model is at capacity.**

## 🐛 Fix: Code Map died on files with duplicate symbol names

Two symbols sharing a `qualifiedName` in one file silently broke navigation for that entire file — TOC, overview ruler, Cmd+K, pins and history all stopped jumping. The scroll gate compared a Set of qnames against an array length, so one duplicate left it permanently one short and it never opened.

This is not a corner case. Two same-label `it("...")` calls in a test file do it, as do a `get`/`set` accessor pair, TS declaration merging (`const X = Schema.Struct(…)` plus `type X = typeof X.Type`), Go's several legal `func init()`, and Rust's `impl Display for Foo` / `impl Debug for Foo` both landing on `Foo>fmt`.

The Code Map rail got a pass at the same time: TOC rows carry a line count and an in/out/self edge tally, the function list and jump trail are tabs instead of a fixed 50/50 split, and long pin names wrap instead of truncating.

## 🐛 Fix: Doc comments render with the symbol they document

A symbol's range came from its declaration node, and tree-sitter keeps leading comments as separate siblings — so the doc comment above `export const Foo` was scooped into a nameless `code` block and one unit of reading rendered as two cards. Leading comment runs now fold into the symbol they're glued to, in the TypeScript, Go and Rust pipelines.

## ✨ New: Recent sessions put the running ones first

The feed was sorted by last-active alone, which buried the two rows actually asking for attention: the run still going, and the run that finished while you were elsewhere. Sessions now group by status — running, then done-but-unread, then the rest — newest-first inside each group, in all three lists that render the feed (sidebar dropdown, search panel, `/m`).

## ✨ New: Copy path and locate-in-tree from history diffs

The file path in a commit's diff view is now actionable: copy the absolute path, or jump to that file in the Explorer tree. The same two actions the file browser already had, in the place you're most likely to want them.

## 🐛 Fix: The file tree no longer snaps to the top when you switch projects

Returning to a project fires a full tree reload (the watch socket is paused while hidden), which swapped `FileTree` out for a loading placeholder — unmounting the scroll container and losing the virtualizer's offset. The placeholder is now first-load only. Context-menu **Refresh** stopped jumping too.

## 🐛 Fix: Status dots didn't match their own chips in dark mode

The dots used the text colour step while the number chip beside them fills from the solid step, so in dark mode an unread dot came out pink next to a deep-red chip — one state reading as two. Every status dot moved to the solid step, including two hand-written copies that were on raw Tailwind colours and tracked no theme at all.

## 📦 Misc: Bundled agent CLIs

Claude **2.1.259** (was 2.1.250) and Codex **0.153.0** (was 0.150.1). Both bumps are purely additive — no export removed or narrowed.

## 🌐 Site: r/opencockpit

There's a subreddit now, linked from the site footer and both READMEs. Issues were the only entry point before, which is a poor fit for questions and show-and-tell.

name: v1.0.269
body:
## 🐛 Fix: `~` and `.` in console file paths

Typing `~/Desktop/report.html` into the console opened a 404. The path isn't absolute, so the URL builders joined the project root in front of it and asked the server for `<cwd>/~/Desktop/report.html`. The browser has no home directory to expand, so the expansion moved to `/apps` — the one layer that knows one — on both the `/apps/local/` path and the file-viewer `?file=` param.

A relative path now resolves against **the console's cwd** rather than the project root, so `./report.html` means what you saw after `cd`. The cwd is snapshotted into the bubble when it's created, so a later `cd` can't re-point a bubble you already opened.

Two adjacent defects had to go with it, or the fix is cosmetic: `cd ~` on the client-side fast path left the console standing in a bogus `<cwd>/~`, and path autocomplete returned bare basenames while the caller replaces the whole typed word — so `ls ~/Des⇥` produced `ls Desktop/`. That one predates tildes entirely (`ls src/comp⇥` → `ls components/`). Suggestions now carry the directory exactly as typed. `../sibling/report.html` also stopped coming back 403: the builders never collapsed `.` / `..`, and a surviving `..` reads as traversal.

## 🐛 Fix: Copy silently failed when Cockpit was opened over the LAN

`navigator.clipboard` only exists in a secure context, so every copy in the app threw when the page was served at `http://<lan-ip>:<port>` — which is exactly how a shared review link gets opened. "Copy link" reported a failure there while the share request itself succeeded, because the error came from the clipboard call, not the network.

One fallback is installed in `boot.js` rather than guarding ~50 call sites, so every existing copy button is fixed and future ones are covered.

## 🐛 Fix: The running indicator went dark while a task was still running

Clicking a session badge posted a status that overwrote the `loading` the orchestrator wrote at run start — one of several ways a stored flag desynced from reality. An explicit stop pinned it on forever, a 409 from the scheduled-task retry wrote over a live run, and a server restart left every in-flight session pulsing.

The stored value is no longer trusted on read: the run registry decides what's running, and a stored `loading` with no live run reads as unread — the run ended without a teardown write, and there's output to look at.

## ✨ New: Deleting a scheduled task asks first

The X in a task card's action row deleted immediately, and the delete is destructive — the entry is spliced out of `state.json` with no tombstone — so one mis-click in a row of six dense icons lost a task's prompt and cron expression for good.

The X now arms the card and the whole icon strip is replaced by **Confirm / Cancel**, so the second click can't land on a neighbouring action. Moving the mouse off the card disarms it. A failed delete also surfaces a toast instead of leaving the card on the board looking like a dead button.

## ✨ New: The console guide lists every file type it can actually preview

The empty-state guide advertised 5 previewable extensions, but the browser bubble routes **11** to the built-in viewer. `webp`, `svg`, `csv` and `tsv` worked all along and were simply undiscoverable — the chip list was hand-written while the truth lived in a regex, and the two drifted. They're one list now, so adding a type updates the matcher and the guide together. Local files also get their own guide row instead of riding along under "Browser".

## ✨ New: Skill cards are a uniform grid, and the whole card previews

A wordy description used to stretch its own cell, so the skills board rendered as ragged columns. Cards are a fixed height now — path clamps to two lines, description to four, argument hint pinned to the bottom — and nothing is lost, since both clamped fields keep a tooltip that shows the full text.

The per-card eye button is gone: the card *is* the preview affordance, keyboard-activatable, with the delete/copy buttons no longer doubling as a preview trigger.

## ⚙️ Internal: Builtin slash commands are now `skills/*.md`

The 11 builtin command prompts lived as TypeScript template literals across 11 files, mirrored a second time by a list in the API route. Editing one meant escaping backticks and `${...}` and remembering to touch two registries that nothing linked.

Each command is now `skills/<cmd>/SKILL.md` inside the package — the same format a user-defined skill uses. The directory set *is* the registry, so adding a builtin is `mkdir skills/<cmd>` plus one file. Everything downstream is unchanged: a same-named user skill still shadows a builtin, and the resolved copy is still written to `~/.cockpit/skills/`.

Two things you may notice: builtin prompts are **English-only** now (`language` still picks the wrapper wording around them), and the dropdown descriptions now come from each file's frontmatter — the i18n keys that used to override them had drifted from the prompts they claimed to describe. Contributors who registered Cockpit's own playbooks by absolute path must re-add them from `docs/skills/`; the published `skills/` directory holds runtime code only.

## 📦 Misc: Jupyter notebook bubbles are gone

The `.ipynb` bubble is removed end to end — the cell renderer, the kernel manager, the `/api/jupyter` routes, the `/ws/jupyter` handler, and the bundled Python bridge, which no longer ships or gets copied by postinstall. Typing a path ending in `.ipynb` now falls through to the shell like any other unrecognized input.

Two things left alone on purpose: existing history entries of that type render as empty command bubbles, and `~/.cockpit/kernels` stays put on machines that already have it.

name: v1.0.268
body:
## ✨ New: Schedule a task from a brand-new chat

The scheduler button used to be gated on a chat that had already been sent to, so setting up a recurring task meant firing off a throwaway message first just to make the button appear. A fresh tab can now schedule directly.

The scheduled-task dialog's message box also gains the same `/` and `@` autocomplete the chat composer has. The dispatcher already expanded a scheduled `/qa …` exactly like a typed one — only the affordance was missing, so the commands and skills you could reach were invisible unless you typed them from memory.

Escape dismisses the autocomplete menu first, and closes the dialog only on a second press.

## ✨ New: Load a quick prompt without sending it

Clicking a quick prompt has always meant "send it now", which is wrong whenever the canned text is a starting point rather than the whole message. A new hover action next to edit/delete writes the prompt into the composer instead.

It appends rather than replaces, so stacking a canned prompt onto something half-typed keeps both, and it stays enabled while a reply is streaming — queueing up the next message is exactly when you want it.

## 🐛 Fix: Git history dropped a real commit at every page boundary

Each page of git history ended in a phantom entry rendered as `NaNy ago · NaN-NaN-NaN NaN:NaN`. That empty record also inflated the page count, so the next page's `--skip` overshot by one and silently swallowed a real commit at every boundary — and "load more" never turned itself off. Verified against a 171-commit repo: pages are now 50/50/50/21, with no gaps and no phantoms.

## 🐛 Fix: Scheduled Codex sessions showed a Claude badge

A scheduled Codex task appeared in the recent-sessions list as Claude, and stayed wrong until you opened it. The engine was only ever recorded from open browser tabs, and a scheduled task never has one. It is now recorded when the task is dispatched, which also covers sessions you never open.

## 🐛 Fix: Slash commands with digit-first names silently no-opped

A skill named `/5e` could be registered, listed by the skills API, and offered by autocomplete — then did nothing at all when sent, with no toast and no log. The verb tokenizer required a leading letter. It now matches up to the first whitespace and leaves the decision to the known-command check, which also unblocks `_`, `:` and `.` in skill names.

## 📦 Misc: Bundled agent CLIs

Claude **2.1.250** (was 2.1.245) and Codex **0.150.1** (was 0.149.1). Both are pinned exactly, so the version you install is the version that was tested.

name: v1.0.267
body:
## ✨ New: The scheduled-task board, rebuilt

The flat card grid is gone. The left column now **groups tasks by what they're waiting for** — finished/unread, armed, paused — each sorted by the time that group is actually read by. A completed task stays with the finished ones even after you read it, instead of pretending it's still upcoming.

The right column **previews the selected task's session**, so you can read what a run produced without leaving the board. Clicking a card only selects it now; navigating into the session moved to the preview header, so a click can't make a row jump between groups under your cursor. An **open-session pill** floats at the transcript's top or bottom edge — wherever your reading actually ends — and fades out in between so it never covers a message.

Editing a task no longer opens a centered dialog: the editor **hangs off the row's Edit button**, flipping and sliding to stay on screen, and repositions itself as the form grows. ESC now closes innermost-first — preview, then editor, then board.

## ✨ New: Step through a conversation question by question

The message list could only jump to the two ends. The bottom capsule now holds **[jump to latest | prev user message | next user message]**, so a long session can be walked one question at a time. Landing is top-aligned, so the reply that follows each message stays in view, and the two buttons grey out at the ends.

## ✨ New: Image diffs in the last two places that lacked them

- **Status pane** — a changed image now renders **before and after side by side**, using the same comparison basis as the text diff (unstaged reads index → working tree, staged reads HEAD → index, a rename reads the before side through its pre-rename name), so the image and the line diff can never disagree about what "before" means.
- **Tool-call snapshot diff** — a PNG that a Bash call rewrote used to show as "binary or oversized file". It now renders as a real image diff. `.svg` keeps its line diff on purpose rather than turning into two rendered copies.

## ✨ New: Fold every long string in a JSON preview at once

The JSON preview could already fold a multi-line string value by clicking it — but a results file with dozens of them took dozens of clicks. A **折叠 / 展开** segmented control now sits in the Explorer toolbar and drives every foldable entry together. Individual clicks still work; the next press supersedes them.

## ✨ New: See which agent CLIs your build bundles

Both Claude Code and Codex ship *inside* their SDKs at a pinned version, so the CLI you were actually running was invisible from the UI — the first thing a bug report needs to state, and the one thing it couldn't. Settings now says it outright:

```
Cockpit v1.0.267
Claude Code 2.1.245 · Codex 0.149.1 · 内置
```

## 🐛 Fix: A 663 KB single-line JSON no longer wedges the tab

Not the file size — Chrome's scroll cost for one un-wrapped line is quadratic in its inline-fragment count, and syntax highlighting turned that file into **53,643 spans on one line**, measuring ~8.8s *per scroll event*. The highlighter now caps at 2000 tokens per line and renders past that as escaped plain text (2000 is the last step that still fits a 60fps frame). Degraded lines keep their exact characters, so column math, selection, search offsets and Cmd+click go-to-definition all stay aligned — what they lose is colour.

The cap lives in the one function every line-rendering surface goes through, so CodeViewer, DiffView, BlockViewer and the References / Search panels are all covered. Measured on the reported file: **53,643 spans → 0, scroll 44,242ms → 2ms.**

## 🐛 Fix: Codex tool-call snapshots

Three bugs that all traced back to the same place:

- **The file-changes panel of a Codex turn listed commits from earlier turns.** Codex restarts its `item_0, item_1, …` counter every turn and its thread id survives resume, so neither pinned a turn — one local repo had 111 commits spanning four days under a single session key. Snapshots now carry the turn's run id. Older commits without one still resolve, so existing history doesn't vanish on upgrade.
- **Exec commands were parsed as JSON when Codex writes JavaScript.** Bare object keys (`cmd:`, not `"cmd":`) threw on the first key, so 659 of 765 scripts in one real rollout classified as unknown, snapshots lost their FileDiff after a refresh, and reloaded transcripts rendered the raw JS wrapper as the command. On the same corpus: **unknown 659 → 2.**
- **`write_stdin` / `update_plan` were mislabelled Bash** with that wrapper in the command header. They now render under their own names.

## 🐛 Fix: The file-changes panel went stale mid-run

The Explorer overlay rendered a copy of the message's tool calls frozen at click time, so anything the AI edited afterwards never appeared. It now follows the message live — while still never reopening a panel you closed, or stealing one showing a different message.

## 🐛 Fix: Failures from the agent CLIs are no longer swallowed

- **Claude's stderr is forwarded into the server log.** The SDK discards the child's stderr unless asked for it, so an unknown flag after a version bump, a libc mismatch, or an outright crash all reached you as a bare `Claude Code process exited with code 1` with the reason already thrown away.
- **Codex's native binary is checked too, not just Claude's.** npm silently skips optional platform binaries during an in-place `npm i -g`. Claude fails loudly; Codex quietly falls back to whatever `codex` is on your PATH — a build its SDK never pinned itself to. That fallback stays (it keeps Codex usable), but it no longer happens in silence.

## 📦 Misc: The agent SDKs are pinned now

`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` was a caret range, so it resolved independently on every install — two people on the same Cockpit version could be running different Claudes depending on the day they installed, with nothing negotiating a protocol version to catch it. It wasn't free either: the platform binary is pinned to the SDK version, so every drift refetched a ~360 MB tarball.

This release pins both (**claude 2.1.245, codex 0.149.1**) so the tested version is the shipped version, and adds `npm run check-agents` plus a weekly PR to keep the pin from going stale.

## 🌐 Site: opencockpit.dev on a phone

The homepage stakes its whole proof on one screenshot, which at 390px rendered its body text at roughly 3px — texture, not information. It's now held at a legible size inside a pannable frame that opens on the agent conversation rather than on window chrome.

The install command was the label of a `<button>`, so you couldn't drag-select it, and its clipboard failure was swallowed — which happens on every non-secure origin, exactly the shared-dev-box HTTP deployment this project advertises. It's a selectable `<code>` beside a real button now, with a fallback, a visible failure state, and `Requires Node 20+ · MIT licensed` underneath.

Also here: Inter is self-hosted instead of hoped-for, selection / caret / scrollbar / focus ring all derive from the palette instead of Chrome's blue, seventeen nav and footer tap targets now clear the WCAG 24×24 minimum, and the Chinese copy was rewritten to read as Chinese rather than as translated English.

name: v1.0.266
body:
## ✨ New: CSV / TSV previews

Open a local `.csv` or `.tsv` from a console bubble and it now renders in the built-in file-viewer, the same route `.md` / `.json` / `.pdf` / images already take. The table view gained the two things a spreadsheet actually needs:

- **Filter** — substring match across all columns, or scope it to one column via the toolbar dropdown.
- **Click-to-sort** — asc → desc → off, numbers compared numerically and empty cells sunk to the bottom. Row numbers stay in file order through both filter and sort.

A **table / raw** toggle sits in the toolbar. One implementation (`window.CockpitCsv`, wrapping the Explorer's table view) now backs the console, the chat modal, and the Explorer pane alike.

## ✨ New: Favorite sessions, on the tab

The tab bar's pushpin becomes a **star**. Click it to add or remove a session from your favorites list — filled gold means favorited, outlined means not. The star lives on the top-right of the tab's number chip (far left of the tab); a tab with no session yet shows none.

The **Favorite Sessions** panel now renders each row from the same parts as the recent-sessions list above it: status dot, engine mark, relative time, live title, last-message preview, current-project highlight, and the full hover card (path + branch + first/last message). A session favorited long ago that has aged out of the recent record degrades gracefully to just its project and title.

One word for the feature everywhere now — **收藏 / favorite** — in both languages, replacing the old mix of "常用 / Pinned / star / 收藏".

## 🐛 Fix: Terminal pipe commands lost your PATH

Pipe (non-pty) console commands spawned a login shell with no `PATH`, so tools installed via an rc-file PATH edit — Android platform-tools, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.cargo/bin`, nvm/pyenv shims — vanished. `adb …` said `command not found` in a pipe bubble while the identical command ran fine in a pty one. Both branches now inherit the server PATH, and a user-supplied `PATH` still wins.

## 🌐 Site: faster landing page

The homepage hero was a 544 KB lazy-loaded PNG with no dimensions — it drove mobile LCP to 5.1s and desktop CLS to 0.153. It's now a 92 KB WebP served eager and preloaded through `next/image`, with the box reserved up front. Two accessibility nits went with it.

```
mobile   Lighthouse 0.81 → 0.97   LCP 5.1s → 2.6s
desktop  Lighthouse 0.91 → 1.00   CLS 0.153 → 0
```
